One of the most fun games I've ever played, It isn't perfect as it can get very grindy in many place of the game, but the loop of hunting monsters, getting better gear to hunt stronger monsters, to get even better gear rarely feels all that tedious because every hunt feel just that little different to spice things. This game has beautiful sights, models and maps, a complicated but mostly intuitive menu system and genuinely good balancing and hit boxes. The story isn't anything to write home about but its interesting enough for a game that is essentially a boss rush with semi-open environments to explore and gather resources. with friends (as with many games) its even more fun, as the game is built with cooperation and coordination with a group just as much if perhaps a bit more then with solo players. Not to mention it have an extremely open and friendly community who are always ready to help new players. In addition to this the dlc expansion Iceborne is actually bigger then the base game and offers more of the same while adding more then enough to justify a new expansion and reward the skills you refined in the base game. if you want a well paced combat focused game that lets you turn your brain off or lock in depending on your mood, or just need something to mess around with your group for hours on end without much muss or fuss. Monster Hunter World is already the game for you. Buy Monster Hunter World:Iceborne, you won't regret. P.S: Stay away from the guardian armor set and defender weapons they completely ruin the base game's progression and you will be very frustrated when you get to Iceborne and suddenly you aren't tanking damage like you used to. They are basically for speed running to the DLC. I made this mistake and nearly rage quit on one of the early bosses in the DLC cuz I just wasn't as good as the game expected me to be due to being carried by Guardian Armor, or Defender gear.

Played The Witcher 3 more times than I can count. All the way back in 2015 on PC(GOG) and I’ve also completed it on PS4. When I heard about the remaster and the new DLC coming out in 2027, I knew I had to go back one more time. Having 100% completed it, I can now safely say this is easily one of the greatest games of all time. No one tells a story quite like CDPR and everyone should experience the Bloody Baron questline at least once in their life. There is truly nothing else like it. That said, the remaster isn't without it's issues. Visual bugs pop up, environments(especially indoors) can be excessively dark and performance takes a hit with ray tracing or path tracing enabled. In Novigrad, the framerate drops to nearly half of what it is elsewhere in the game. Going for all the achievements was also a headache, particularly with Gwent cards tied to NPC's that occasionally become unresponsive. These bugs have been around since day one and have never been fixed. Still, these are minor complaints for a game that remains pure joy.

I really don't get the hype, it's a grindy game that has quick and slippery controls with combat that is way too fast and chaotic and gameplay that gets really repetitive Before you judge me, I've played roguelikes, I know what to expect, Inscryption, Hades, Isaac, ETG, all examples of great games that are very clear and understandable In a nutshell, usually, you'll have way too many things happening on screen at once, which would make you maximize your damage so you don't have to deal with dodging attacks And that's the biggest problem, it's trying to be a fast paced game without really nailing what makes a fast game work, it has annoying side missions, missing keys, obscure shortcuts, and so many dead ends. Neither are the bosses or the elite encounters fun, felt like they were really basic in their design, and you would kill them only if you get lucky with good build, without really requiring any sort of skill or strategy And as for visuals, despite the pixel art being detailed, everything in the world was all blending into one another to really not give you any sort of visual clarity during fights Most of all, I hate it's DLCs, and how they shove these in your face in many of the doors you get to, I've encountered them throughout my third playthrough and it just felt like a mobile F2P game at some points If you were to ask me, if it looks interesting to you, buy it, and judge it based on the first hour, as it wouldn't get any more interesting than that, otherwise, just refund it, don't keep it like I did expecting something else With the overwhelmingly positive reviews I was sure I was missing something, but it doesn't seem like it, so if it wasn't clear, no, I wouldn't really recommend the game, but I would encourage you to try it if it seems interesting

The graphics/art is amazing yes we know, but the longer I've played this game the more repetitive it has felt.
